question: What does the key signature tell you that the notes do not?
intro: An accented, repeated B begins a lullaby, with one sharp in the key signature. The middle part has four sharps and is marked pp; the opening shape then returns and the piece ends on a held chord.

sections.label: B · four sharps, E major, pp
A′ · the lullaby returns
sections.mNote: opening shape again, ending on a fermata chord

cues.title: An accented, repeated note
cues.text: Two beats to the bar, one sharp in the key signature, marked p. The tune starts on a repeated B with accent marks, over a left-hand figure that circles the same few notes. The eight bars are written out as two groups of four that are nearly identical on the page.
cues.evidence: First edition p. 18 (IMSLP #03060): 2/4, one sharp, p, repeated B with > accents, left-hand figure on the same chord tones; the first two systems are identical in notation. Report: B region with F♯ and C among the strongest pitch classes at 0:05–0:20; 2.0–2.6 onsets per second.
cues.how: Placed from the score’s proportions; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: Four sharps: the middle part
cues.text: After a double bar the key signature jumps from one sharp to four, for E major, and the marking drops to pp. The report’s key estimates change around 0:35–0:45. At one point the right hand moves into the bass clef.
cues.evidence: Report: novelty 0.31 at 0:28; pitch classes E♭ (D♯) C♯ B at 0:40 and B major at 0:40–0:55; −15.4 dB at 0:40. Score p. 18, third system: key signature of four sharps, pp, a clef change to bass in the right-hand part. Machine keys are confirmation only.

cues.title: Memories of childhood, written for adults
cues.text: Schumann was twenty-seven in February 1838 and would not marry Clara for another two and a half years. He called the cycle reflections of an older person for older people, not music for children to play.
cues.evidence: Henle Urtext review at schumann-portal.de/3213.html: Schumann’s “Rückspiegelungen eines älteren für ältere” and the remark that the pieces are for adults who remember childhood; Zwickau catalogue, item 11, gives the phrase as “eines Erwachsenen für Ältere”. Born 8 June 1810, so twenty-seven in February–March 1838. The marriage took place on 12 September 1840 (Clara Schumann, Wikipedia; composer page).

cues.title: The lullaby returns
cues.text: Near 1:12 the repeated B comes back, p again, and the key signature returns to one sharp. The report finds its largest boundary here, and the rate of attacks nearly halves.
cues.evidence: Report: novelty 1.00 at 1:12; −9.8 dB at 1:05, −11.9 dB at 1:10, onsets 1.2 per second at 1:10 against 2.2 at 1:05. Score p. 19, third system: one-sharp key signature, p, repeated B.

cues.title: Ritardando, then a held chord
cues.text: The last system is marked ritardando and ends on a chord with a fermata. The report’s key estimate for the last windows is A minor (r = 0.77–0.86), not the E minor of the opening, so the chord does not simply come home. The sound falls from −17 dB at 1:40 to −43 dB at 1:55.
cues.evidence: Report: −16.8 dB at 1:40, −22.4 dB at 1:45, −28.5 dB at 1:50, −42.6 dB at 1:55, −61.9 dB at 2:00; 0.4 onsets per second at 1:50. Score p. 19, last system: ritardando over the final bars, fermata chord. Key estimates: A minor 1:45–2:00, against E-based harmony in the first system (Em chord, then a chord with D♯); machine keys are confirmation only.

transitions.title: Key signature changes at the double bar
transitions.to: B · four sharps, E major, pp
transitions.how: The first eight bars end on a double bar, and the key signature changes from one sharp to four. The music moves from E minor to E major with no modulating bridge, and the marking drops to pp. The left-hand rocking continues, so the change of colour comes while the motion stays the same.
transitions.evidence: Score p. 18: double bar after the second system, four-sharp key signature and pp in the third. Report: novelty 0.31 at 0:28; E♭ C♯ B pitch classes and B major at 0:40–0:55.

transitions.title: A ritardando, then one sharp again
transitions.from: B · four sharps, E major, pp
transitions.how: The middle part ends with a ritardando and the key signature returns to one sharp. The repeated B and the left-hand figure of the opening are heard again, and the harmony leaves the E-major region of the middle part for the one-sharp harmony of the opening.
transitions.evidence: Score p. 19, second to third systems: ritard., change to one sharp, p. Report: novelty 1.00 at 1:12, level −11.9 dB at 1:10 and onsets halving from 2.2 to 1.2 per second.

composer.epithet: His music lets remembered fragments, concealed names and competing inner voices interrupt the forms that contain them.
facts: Piano with Friedrich Wieck; composition with Heinrich Dorn; extensive private study of Bach and Beethoven
Co-founder of the Neue Zeitschrift für Musik, 1834; editor until 1844
Married Clara Wieck in 1840; eight children, seven surviving infancy
Leipzig Conservatoire teacher; municipal music director, Düsseldorf, 1850–53
composer.background:
Schumann grew up in Zwickau, where his father August was a bookseller and publisher. Reading and music developed together: Jean Paul’s novels, with their interruptions, doubles and changes of narrative voice, mattered alongside piano lessons. Sent to Leipzig to study law in 1828, he spent more time on music and literature; a period in Heidelberg did not reconcile him to a legal career. He returned to Leipzig to study piano seriously with Friedrich Wieck. Wieck’s daughter Clara, already performing publicly as a child, gave him an immediate example of the professional discipline he hoped to acquire.

A persistent problem with his right hand ended the prospect of a virtuoso career. The familiar account of a finger-strengthening device leaves the injury’s medical cause uncertain. Composition and criticism became his principal occupations. The early published piano works already had distinct literary and formal premises: the Abegg Variations derive a theme from letters, while Papillons relates its dances to the masked-ball ending of Jean Paul’s Flegeljahre. The miniatures’ sudden juxtapositions recreate the experience of a narrative changing speakers and levels.
